component.name: LinuxFiles
component.summary: Files for Linux, a modern file manager

description.p: LinuxFiles, Files for Linux, is based on Files by the Files Community. It is a modern file manager with tabs, a dual-pane view, column and grid layouts, tags, previews and archive support. LinuxFiles is an unofficial, community-maintained Linux port of Files by the Files Community, built on the Uno Platform and not affiliated with or endorsed by the Files Community.
This port is under active development and is not yet feature complete.

developer.name: LinuxFiles contributors (fork of Files by Files Community)

description.p: Tags are preserved when extended-attribute writes fail on read-only files, including across reloads, restarts, export and import (fixes issue #148).
Context-menu models are built off the UI thread, with stale-menu and placement fixes, selection improvements and reduced UI stalls.

Upstream-sync preparation adds a Windows path allowlist and guarded prune helper; no Windows files have been removed yet. The sync workflow updates existing branches and pull requests. The Rust backend benchmark is a documented no-go; the application keeps its C# backend.

Known limits: select-all in folders with 10,000 items remains slow due to Uno selection handling. Text and icons can remain blurry on XWayland without the compositor scale setting or UNO_DISPLAY_SCALE_OVERRIDE; issue #113 remains open.

Tags now persist across folder reloads and app restarts: Linux now loads saved row properties. Tag edits merge correctly with saved tags, and opening a zip no longer requires two Back presses. Layout switches are faster on Linux with a lightweight selection checkbox.

The experimental Detect display scale from the compositor setting can sharpen text on niri/xwayland-satellite when no display or toolkit scale is configured. It is off by default and requires a restart. UNO_DISPLAY_SCALE_OVERRIDE also works and takes precedence; some setups may double-scale. New pixelation documentation covers XWayland upscaling and Uno font hinting limits.

Archive navigation and extraction progress fixes, system cursor preferences and a corrected Status Center icon, cached context-menu parsing and queued tag writes, compositor-aware backdrop modes and System colours, an opt-in NixOS root-actions module with a runtime-capability check, and fewer Windows-only assets in Linux builds.

Known limits: X11/XWayland only, slow select-all in folders with 10,000 items due to Uno selection handling, and possible lost tags after successive edits on read-only tagged files when extended-attribute writes fail (issue #148).

Optional Adwaita-style appearance, a working app background image and window opacity, a fix for the glitching tab bar icon, faster rendering on systems without GPU acceleration, a Nix flake and safer root helper installation.

First public alpha of LinuxFiles. Faster grouped views, KDE service menus, optional root actions and root mode, native file pickers, opening files inside archives and a client-side title bar with tabs.
